title: Converting a Toilet to Dual-Flush: Retrofit, Valve Installation, and Bowl Refilling

locations.name: bathroom
locations.basis: Explicit reference to 'this bathroom down here' and discussion of the toilet location; no confirmation of shooting location

summary: This Old House walks a homeowner through converting an existing 3.5 gallons-per-flush toilet into a dual-flush model using a retrofit valve and a two-button actuator. The video covers removing the old tank lever, installing a dual-flush valve with a blue gasket, attaching a two-button actuator (one for liquids, one for solids), and reconfiguring the fill valve to ensure the bowl refills adequately after a reduced liquid flush. The host demonstrates turning off the water, draining the tank, wiring and securing components, and then testing a liquid flush that uses significantly less water while preserving a full flush for solids. A noted tradeoff is that the bowl needs adequate refill water, prompting a later adjustment with an adjustable fill valve and refill tube to restore proper bowl performance. The segment ends with a recap of how to use the top (liquids) and bottom (solids) buttons and the expected water savings.
